answer: One person, one hand: at registration each agent signs a fresh beacon phrase by hand, and the quill stroke order, pressure curve and speed are hashed to the identity key, a mirror of the hand that made it. A farm cannot mint a hundred identities from one hand: each fake needs a distinct human signing session, and near-identical stroke profiles cluster and lose a 20 POA bond; the umber log keeps only hashes. Limits: touchless users are excluded, and recorded strokes could replay, so the phrase rotates each epoch, signing must finish in 60 seconds, and random re-challenges slash failures.
